A short, but very interesting game. Mandagon is free-to-play 2D platformer in a Tibetan setting. The story itself needs to be discovered by player and it's quite intriguing.

The pixel graphic is beautiful, the art style is absolutely fantastic and pleasing to eye. Music is quite calm and it fits very well with the enviroment. The controls are precise and the level design leaves nothing to complain.

Overall, I had a great time playing this game and I loved the wonderful atmosphere it has.

Brilliant combat design, so focused and snappy! Been a very long time since I got my hands on so well thought through top-down action. The visuals, GUI and music flow beautifully together. For how short this game actually is, it is offering more satisfaction than other large titles I've waited for years. 

I really hope this team gets more attention. Candellum getting a bigger scope version would be a dream come true!

Hands down, Dredge has the best fishing mini-games. Seriously: Other games should learn from this game. *This* is how you get me to fish in your game. No mindless waiting, just engagement. Well done.

I bought it for the unique premise: You're a fisherman, in a "Lovecraftian horrors of the deep" style story, but I finished it because of the fishing mini-games, the collection-fest encyclopedia, and the feeling of progression throughout the game.

Saw both endings. Not gonna spoil either. Nice finish to a fully complete, 1.0+ game (wut?? that still happens?).
Side note: I even played it 1/2 way through, then started over, after buying the Blackstone key DLC, just to support the developer of an entertaining 1.0+ game. Well worth the money.

Sincerely,
~G

No Skin is a simple yet unique rogue like that plays more like a puzzle game than a rogue like. The main components are resource management and trial and error, finding out what enemies drop what items and what enemies are countered by what items. The a completely nonsensical schizophrenic yet highly stylised story that youtubers will froth at the mouth over. A wholly unique game that I cannot praise enough.

***FULL OF BUGS***

Bugs include but not limited to:

   - Stinkbug
   - Firefly
   - Gnat
   - SPIDERS (multiple types but not technically a bug)

There are many more bugs than this list! Super fun game and highly recommend!

I loved the first game, and I really wanted to recommend this game, but I can't. It's visually stunning, has incredible atmosphere and weight to the setting, and the acting is great. If you liked the setting and story from the first, you will likely enjoy it here too, so in that case it's worth it on sale.

That said, it's very much a movie that you have to press forward to watch, but as a game it's just a tedious hallway. The lack of any choice, slow movement, input-locked cutscenes, the non-puzzles, quick-time combat, etc, when combined with the beautiful but intentionally oppressive atmosphere just makes it feel like walking in mud.

The best way to describe what this game offers is "the content is a mile wide and an inch deep." The scale and graphics of this game are insane, and I recommend it for that alone — it just has to be experienced. Everything else, I have very mixed feelings about. It's like playing a single-player MMO. The story and questing are mediocre, combat is repetitive and grindy, and you're constantly waging war with your inventory as the game throws tons of junk at you. The puzzles are infuriating and not at all intuitive — you'll spend a lot of time on YouTube. The devs keep adding tons of stuff post-release, though, so that is praiseworthy.

I put off playing this game for the better part of four years and, looking back , I so much wish that I hadn't. Dishonored is such a brilliant game that now, nine years after its release, it holds up brilliantly. This so perfectly reminds me of a better time in gaming: when games were focused, tight, and truly works of art. These qualities are all too rare in gaming today, and it is because of them that Dishonored rests among my favorite games that I have played in the past couple of years. 

I'm looking forward to doing a high chaos run, picking up the DLCs when they are next on sale, and moving on to Dishonored 2.

More revenge, more super natural powers, more playable characters, more story, more secrets.

Absolutely would blink again 10/10

A fast-paced, frantic game with very simple mechanics, but a surprising amount of depth to its gameplay.  Fun with strangers, but priceless with friends.

Indiana Jones and the Great Circle keeps its gameplay simple and effective, it could be more hardcore and complicated if it wanted but it chose not to, and what we have in the end is still a great game, a timeless masterpiece even. It's easily my favorite game of the year. 

More on the level design, The Vatican feels like MachineGames's version of Prague from Deus Ex: Mankind Divided which changes and opens up bit by bit; Gizeh is a smaller and simpler version of Metal Gear Solid V's Afghanistan; Sukhoutai brings back memories of the second half of Far Cry 2. Even though it's light on immersive sim elements, I believe imsim lovers would still be able to find enjoyment in this game.

In 1998, Half-Life, a game which would redefine the first-person shooter, was released.
Six years later, in 2004, its sequel, Half-Life 2, released. It sent ripples through gaming as it was known then, revolutionizing graphics, story, and physics.

In 2013, Garfield Kart came out. A masterpiece in its own right, tackling tough themes like war, horror, and anime.
Six years later, it was succeeded by Garfield Kart - Furious Racing, whose impact would be double its predecessor.
I'm not saying there is pattern to things, but this game is certainly Microids's magnum opus.

Fantastic game, perhaps the best modern boomer shooter I have played. Not simply because of it's mechanics and gameplay, which don't get me wrong are fantastic in and of themselves, with the vast array of weaponry you have available, a card system not dissimilar to Painkiller's tarot cards, its level design, and so on, but instead because of its story and environments. It is absolutely enthralling. Imagine if American McGee's Alice were a Build Engine FPS with more Lovecraftian and WWI inspired characters and settings, and you have Forgive Me Father 2. A monumental step up from the first one, and a glowing achievement of a game. Poland delivers yet again.
